headline: `b.guardCsv` reads a document under every delimiter a consumer might use, and its sanitize disarms or refuses
summary: The CSV guard split cells on every delimiter it knows at once, while a consumer reads with one, so a formula cell that a comma reader or a tab reader sees could sit inside a cell the guard read as quoted. Each candidate delimiter is now its own reading and every finding any reading produces is reported. `sanitize()` never disarmed a formula cell and returned one the operator had set to refuse; it now disarms under a prefixing policy and refuses under `reject` and for a denylisted function. The profiles' default mitigation moves from a TAB prefix to the single-quote prefix, which holds under every delimiter reading. Upgrading requires no code change; a CSV emitted through the guard carries `'` where it carried a TAB in front of a formula-shaped cell, and `prefix-tab` remains selectable for tab-separated output.

items.title: `b.guardCsv` reads a document under each delimiter separately
items.body:
The cell walk treated `,`, `;`, TAB and `|` as delimiters at the same time. A consumer reads with one of them, and the two structures differ around quotes: to a comma reader `a;"x` followed by a newline and `""=1` is text, a record end, and then an empty quoted section with `=1` after it, which every RFC 4180 reader including `b.csv.parse` yields as the cell `=1`, a live formula. The guard split at the `;`, read the quote as opening a quoted cell, and carried that cell across the newline, so the formula rule never saw the cell and strict validation reported nothing. The same shape hid from the guard behind a TAB or a `|` a comma reader does not split on, and behind a comma a tab reader does not.

The guard now walks the document once per candidate delimiter (`,`, `;`, TAB, `|`, and the operator's own) and reports what any reading finds: a formula cell, a denylisted function, and the residual check that decides whether a sanitized document can be served. One cell is one finding however many readings expose it.

items.title: `b.guardCsv.sanitize` disarms a formula cell or refuses it
items.body:
`sanitize()` stripped characters and returned the document, so a formula cell came back as written, under `formulaInjectionPolicy: "reject"` too, and a denylisted `=WEBSERVICE(...)` came back as written at every profile, while the function's own documentation promised it never returns a class the operator asked it to refuse. It now refuses a formula cell under `reject`, a denylisted function, and mixed line endings under `dialectPolicy: "strict"`, each with the finding's rule id. Under a prefixing policy it disarms a formula cell the way the gate does: the document is re-parsed, re-serialized with the prefix inside a quoted field, and read again under every delimiter; a cell that is still a formula under one of those readings is refused rather than served. The gate serves what `sanitize` returns.

The mitigated form of a denylisted function is still the denylisted function. `"'=WEBSERVICE(...)"` and, under `prefix-tab`, `"<TAB>=WEBSERVICE(...)"` validated clean; Excel drops the leading apostrophe when it saves and re-opens the file, and the gate refuses a denylisted call even prefixed. The denylist walk reads through the guard's own prefixes now, in either order with the leading whitespace it also reads through.

items.title: A denylisted call anywhere in a formula cell is refused
items.body:
The denylist read the one word after the trigger, so `=SUM(HYPERLINK(A1))`, `=1+WEBSERVICE("http://x/")`, `=(WEBSERVICE(...))`, `="x"&WEBSERVICE(...)` and `= WEBSERVICE(...)` validated with only the formula finding, which a prefixing policy sanitizes rather than refuses, and `sanitize()` served them prefixed. The walk now reads the whole cell as the consumer decodes it under each delimiter reading, including the text after a closing quote, and reports the first denylisted call it finds anywhere in the cell, outside a string, a quoted sheet name or a structured reference. A call under Excel's `_xlfn.` or `_xlws.` namespace names the same function (`=_xlfn.WEBSERVICE(...)` is `WEBSERVICE`), and a tab or a line break between a name and its parenthesis is read as the space it is. A name that begins after a digit or a letter is still read as a call: no evaluator runs `=1HYPERLINK(...)`, and refusing it costs no formula that runs.

Under `formulaInjectionPolicy: "allowlist"`, a formula cell that only another delimiter's reading exposes cannot be re-serialized away, and the residual check exempted such a cell on its leading call alone, so `safe;=SUM(FOO(A1))` was served to a semicolon reader with only `SUM` allowlisted. The residual is now served only when every call in it is allowlisted, the rule `escapeCell` already applied to the cells it can rewrite.

items.title: `POSITIVE_NUMBER_OPTS` on every guard, and `positiveNumberOpts` on `b.gateContract.defineGuard` and `resolveProfileAndPosture`
items.body: A guard's ratio and threshold options are declared the way its integer caps are declared in `INT_OPTS`. The resolver holds each one to a positive finite number, with fractions allowed, and exempts it from the integer checks. `b.guardCsv` and `b.guardText` declare `sanitizeAmplificationCap`; `b.guardDomain` declares `dgaEntropyThreshold`. A guard built by `defineGuard` that names a `sanitizeAmplificationCap` field declares it without being asked.

items.title: `b.guardCsv.sanitize` re-parses a document under the guard's own caps
items.body: The disarm step re-parses through `b.csv.parse`, whose defaults (16 MiB of input, 1 MiB per field) are not the guard's (`maxTotalBytes` 1 GiB, `maxCellBytes` 64 KiB), so an export within the guard's limits failed with the parser's `csv/too-large` when, and only when, a formula cell required mitigation. The parser now runs under `maxTotalBytes`, `maxRows` and `maxCellBytes`, a cap it hits is reported as the guard's own `csv.total-too-large`, `csv.too-many-rows` or `csv.cell-too-large`, and a document the emitted dialect cannot parse is refused as `csv.formula-injection` rather than surfacing another module's error.

items.title: A line break inside a quoted cell is content, for the dialect rule and for the trailing-whitespace trim
items.body: `dialect-mixed-line-endings` counted every CR and LF in the text, so a CRLF document carrying a multi-line quoted cell, which `b.csv.parse` reads as one record, was refused as a mixed dialect; `b.guardCsv.detect` reported the same document as `mixed`. Both read record ends under the configured delimiter and quote now: a line break inside a quoted cell is content, and a quote in the middle of an unquoted cell is text, so the line break after it is still a record end. `trailingWhitespacePolicy: "trim"` split the text on LF alone, so on a CRLF document, the guard's own default line ending, the CR was the last character of every line and nothing was trimmed, while inside a quoted multi-line cell the content was trimmed and the junk after its closing quote was kept. The trim now strips the horizontal whitespace at the end of each record, under CRLF, LF or CR, and leaves the inside of a quoted cell alone.

items.title: `b.guardCsv.serialize` resolves its options once per document
items.body: Every cell merged the guard's defaults into a fresh options object before it was escaped. A 17 MiB export of three million cells spent 20 seconds in that merge; it now serializes in under one.

items.title: A ratio or threshold option refuses a value it cannot compare against
items.body: `sanitizeAmplificationCap` on `b.guardCsv` and `b.guardText` and `dgaEntropyThreshold` on `b.guardDomain` accepted `Infinity`, `NaN`, a string, a negative number and zero. Each comparison against such a value is false, so an infinite cap removed the limit and a `NaN` threshold switched the DGA heuristic off while the option stayed set. Each now throws the guard's `bad-opt` error at the call that sets it. The integer caps already refused these shapes, and the check that did so was derived from the shape of an option's default, which is why a fractional default was never checked and a whole-number default would have refused the fraction a ratio takes.

items.title: The profiles' formula mitigation is `prefix-quote`
items.body:
`strict`, `balanced` and `permissive` prefixed a formula-shaped cell with a TAB inside the quoted field. A TAB is the delimiter of a tab-separated reader, and such a reader of a comma document with more than one column takes the quote and comma before the TAB as text and splits at the TAB: `b.csv.parse` with `delimiter: "\t"` reads `"alice","<TAB>=cmd|x"` as the cells `alice,"` and `=cmd|x"`, a live formula. The single-quote prefix holds under every delimiter reading and is the mitigation OWASP lists first. OWASP also notes that Excel drops it when it saves and re-opens the file, so the TAB prefix remains selectable as `formulaInjectionPolicy: "prefix-tab"` for tab-separated output, where it holds. A document sanitized under `prefix-tab` that a tab-separated reading would still evaluate is refused rather than served as disarmed.

`|` is no longer a formula trigger: no spreadsheet evaluator opens a formula on it and it is on no published list, so a cell such as `|x` is emitted as it is and is not a finding. A leading TAB, CR or LF is read through to the character after it, as an importer that trims leading whitespace evaluates what follows: `<TAB>=cmd` is a formula and `<TAB>hello` is text, which also stops a tab-separated file whose first cell is an empty quoted section from being refused under the comma reading. Text after a closing quote is read as part of the cell, as the parsers read it.

items.title: Vendored `@blamejs/pki` moves to 0.7.41
items.body: The vendored bundle rises from 0.7.39 to 0.7.41. `pki.est.serverkeygen` proves a server-generated private key is the private half of the certificate it binds it to with the key itself and refuses a mismatch with `est/key-cert-mismatch`; `pki.crmf.build` proves the key enclosed in an `encryptedKey` proof of possession the same way and refuses with `crmf/bad-popo` a key that only states the template's public components. `pki.pkcs12.build` refuses a `{ key, cert }` pair whose key is not the private half of the certificate's public key, and a key bag and a certificate bag sharing a `localKeyId` whose key is not that certificate's, across every safe of the store, proving the pair with the private material rather than the public components a private key carries about itself; a store carrying one `localKeyId` on two key bags, more than 1024 certificate bags under one key, or more than 1024 safes is refused. A finite-field Diffie-Hellman key pair is proven by the public value its exponent generates in either encoding (PKCS #3 or X9.42), held to a 4096-bit group whose modulus and stated order are prime, and a store links at most 8 such pairs. The package continues to declare no dependencies and no install, prepare or prepublish scripts.

items.title: `b.guardCsv`'s `sanitizeAmplificationCap` is measured on the served output and defaults to 4
items.body: The cap was measured on the character-stripped text before the formula re-serialization, so an operator's cap did not bound the one transform that grows a document. It is measured on what `sanitize()` returns now. The re-serialization quotes every cell, which grows a document of one-character cells 2.25x and one of blank rows 3.25x, so the default moves from 1.5 to 4; a document that grows past the cap is refused with `csv/sanitize-amplified`, and the gate refuses rather than serves it. An operator who set the cap below 2 will see short-celled documents with a formula cell refused where they were served.
